chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Sa'dan ibn Muslim from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the Words of Allah the Exalted, 'And do not display their ornaments except what appears thereof.' He said: 'The ring, and the bracelet, and it is the anklet.'
ai.seo_question: What does 'except what appears thereof' mean in Surah An-Nur according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a specific exegetical interpretation of 'what appears thereof' in Surah An-Nur, identifying the ring (khatam), bracelet (masakah), and anklet as permissible adornments. This view highlights the Shia scholarly tradition of distinguishing between general modesty and specific, culturally recognized ornaments that do not constitute 'zeenah' (beauty/adornment) in the context of the hijab command. The interpretation underscores the balance between preserving modesty and allowing natural, visible accessories in public or semi-public settings.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Is’haq, from Sa’dan Bin Muslim, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,
‘I asked himasws about the Words of Allahazwj the Exalted [24:31] and do not display their ornaments except what appears thereof. Heasws said: ‘The ring, and the bracelet and the anklet’.
en.sarwar: 4. Al-Husayn from Muhammad has narrated from Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Sa‘dan ibn Muslim from abu Basir who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the words of Allah, most High, ‘. . . they must not show off their beauty except for what is exposed.’ [24:32]
He (the Imam) said, ‘It is the items like ring, anklet and bracelet.’”
